translationRepairs: In Chengsheng year 3 (553) he was made bright-prestige general and roaming-cavalry general, raised to marquis with five hundred households.
In Chengsheng year 3 (554) he was made bright-prestige general and roaming-cavalry general, raised to marquis with five hundred households.
承聖三年 with Chengsheng 1 = AD 552 is AD 554; the parenthetical (553) is off by one.
Xiao Bo sent Ouyang Bao against him. Faqu met him in battle and broke his force.
Xiao Bo sent Ouyang Wei against him. Faqu met him in battle and broke his force.
歐陽頠 is Ouyang Wei (498–563), father of 歐陽紇 Ouyang He; Bao is wrong, but the proposal would conflate father and son.
Xiao Bo sent Ouyang Bao to attack Faqu; Faqu fought him and defeated him.
Xiao Bo sent Ouyang Wei to attack Faqu; Faqu fought him and defeated him.
The literal field likewise requires Ouyang Wei for 歐陽頠, keeping him distinct from his son Ouyang He (歐陽紇).

In the second year of Yongding, Wang Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang to attack Zhou Di and also plotted to capture Faqu; Faqu led troops to aid Di and captured Xiaoxiang and three other generals.

In the second year of Yongding, Wang Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoqing to attack Zhou Di and also plotted to capture Faqu; Faqu led troops to aid Di and captured Xiaoqing and the other two generals.
孝頃等三將 means Xiaoqing and the other two generals, three total; 頃 is qing, so 余孝頃 is Yu Xiaoqing rather than Yu Xiaoxiang.
When Emperor Wen took the throne, Faqu's title was raised to pacify-south general.
When Emperor Wen took the throne, Faqu's title was raised to secure-south general.
安南將軍 is a different title from the earlier 平南將軍; collapsing both to "pacify-south" erases the advancement. "secure-south" restores the distinction.
In Tianjia year 2 (563) Zhou Di rebelled. Faqu led his men to join area commander Wu Mingche and fought Di at Gongtang.
In Tianjia year 2 (561) Zhou Di rebelled. Faqu led his men to join area commander Wu Mingche and fought Di at Gongtang.
天嘉二年 with Tianjia 1 = AD 560 is AD 561; the parenthetical (563) is wrong.

When the Founder took the throne, Liang was made credential-holder, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and pacify-west grand general, with pipes and drums and his command and inspectorship unchanged.

When the Founder received the abdication, Liang was made credential-holder, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and pacify-west grand general, with pipes and drums and his command and inspectorship unchanged.
受襌 (for 受禪) means receiving the abdication, not a generic "took the throne"; the proposed wording matches the Chinese technical sense and the literal.
When Jiao was pacified, he also reduced Zhou general the Senior Duke Tuo Ba Ding and others.
When Jiao was pacified, he also reduced Zhou general the Senior Duke Tuoba Ding and others.
拓跋 is the single ethnonym Tuoba; spacing it as Tuo Ba invents a two-part personal name.
沌 is Dun (as in 沌口); Chun is the wrong romanization for this graph.
Literal likewise misreads 沌 as Chun; Dun is the correct reading.
Collation lemma 沌 is again Dun, not Chun; the repair matches the graph.
Same collation unit: 沌 romanizes as Dun; Chun is incorrect in the literal field too.
